subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Attention as a Scarce Resource
description: One-minute skill: Attention as a Scarce Resource.

hook.text: A poker player watches six opponents, the pot, the cards, and a TV screen.

buildup.text: Attention is limited. In complex games, players can't track all relevant information, so they focus on salient cues.

discovery.text: Gabaix showed that limited attention explains pricing anomalies. If consumers can't process all product attributes.

twist.text: Strategic opponents can overload your attention deliberately. Complex contracts, long menus, and rapid decisions all.

climax.text: Simplify your decisions. When overwhelmed, focus on the 2 or 3 most important factors.

punchline.text: You cannot watch everything. Choose what to watch wisely.

quiz.question: How can opponents exploit limited attention?
options: By simplifying their strategies for transparency
By creating complexity that overloads decision-making
By reducing the number of choices available
